title: osquery host posture snapshot
description: One endpoint's posture as reported by osquery / Fleet. v1.3 adds capacity (disk_used_percent, memory_used_percent, cpu_p95_5m_percent), host_role, antimalware_protected and edr_healthy, each with a *_source when it comes from an operator-named Fleet label or policy, and makes every *_source present only alongside its value (dependentRequired). v1.2 added firewall_source and screen_lock_source. Fleet's Get host API has no firewall, screen-lock, memory-use, CPU-use, antimalware or EDR field, so a Fleet-sourced record carries firewall, screen lock, antimalware and EDR only when the operator names a Fleet policy for each, and never carries memory or CPU use. v1.1 added last_seen_at (the host's own last check-in, which observed_at is not) and reason. A posture field is present only when the connector read it: false means observed off, and an absent key means not read.

disk_encryption_enabled.description: Absent when the source did not report it. Fleet omits it when it does not know the status, and for Linux hosts reporting an unencrypted root volume.

screen_lock_enabled.description: Absent when the source did not report it. On a Fleet-sourced record, present only when the operator named a screen-lock Fleet policy and the host's result for it is pass (true) or fail (false); screen_lock_source names the policy.

firewall_enabled.description: Absent when the source did not report it. On a Fleet-sourced record, present only when the operator named a firewall Fleet policy and the host's result for it is pass (true) or fail (false); firewall_source names the policy.

mdm_enrolled.description: From Fleet's mdm.enrollment_status: true for "On (...)", false for "Off" or "Pending", absent otherwise.

last_seen_at.description: When the host last checked in (Fleet's seen_time). The record's observed_at is when the connector pulled, and Fleet lists offline hosts too.

reason.description: Why the result is what it is, e.g. which posture fields were not reported, or the Fleet error from the detail fetch.

firewall_source.description: Where firewall_enabled was read from: fleet_policy:<policy name>. Present only alongside firewall_enabled.

screen_lock_source.description: Where screen_lock_enabled was read from: fleet_policy:<policy name>. Present only alongside screen_lock_enabled.

disk_used_percent.description: Percent of the host's disk in use, 0-100. From Fleet: 100 minus percent_disk_space_available. Absent when not read.

memory_used_percent.description: Percent of the host's memory in use, 0-100, when it was read. Fleet's host API has no memory-use field, so a Fleet-sourced record never carries it. Absent when not read.

cpu_p95_5m_percent.description: 95th percentile of the host's CPU utilisation over the last 5 minutes, 0-100. Neither Fleet's host API nor a single osquery snapshot provides it, so the osquery connector never emits it; a pusher that samples CPU may. Absent when not read.

host_role.description: The host's role: production when the host carries the operator-named production Fleet label, which host_role_source names. Absent when the role was not read, including a host without the label.

host_role_source.description: Where host_role was read from: fleet_label:<label name>. Present only alongside host_role.

antimalware_protected.description: Anti-malware is active with current definitions, as the operator's named Fleet policy defines it: the policy's query holds the engine and the definitions-age bound. true for a pass, false for a fail, absent when not read. antimalware_source names the policy.

antimalware_source.description: Where antimalware_protected was read from: fleet_policy:<policy name>. Present only alongside antimalware_protected.

edr_healthy.description: An EDR or behavioural detection agent is installed, running and healthy, as the operator's named Fleet policy defines it. true for a pass, false for a fail, absent when not read. edr_source names the policy.

edr_source.description: Where edr_healthy was read from: fleet_policy:<policy name>. Present only alongside edr_healthy.
